packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - unverified image reading

Exposure / compliance statement
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author for this packet.
- I opened only PROMPT.md (identical text in each packet; read once in packet-01) and the image files of this packet. One directory listing of my three assigned packet directories was run to learn filenames; packet.json was not read. No web or search.

WORKING NOTES (appended tile by tile)

image-001.jpg (reduced overview, face A)
- Narrow vertical parchment strip, c. 4.5 cm wide x c. 21 cm tall by the scale, upright as presented. A vertical fold/sewing line with small holes c. 1 cm in from the left edge. Left of and across that fold: a column of line-ENDS in pale brown ink (c. 25+ lines), cut by the left edge. The broad middle zone is blank parchment with a vertical grey offset/stain band and several holes (spine-fold wear?). At the right edge, lower third: line-BEGINNINGS of another column, single letters only, including a larger capital "S". Red pigment patches at upper right, right edge and along the left edge (offset or smeared red paint; not rubrics as far as can be seen).
- Tentative interpretation: the strip is cut from the gutter area of a bifolium or from the intercolumn of a two-column page: ends of one column at left, blank intercolumn/gutter, beginnings of the next column at right.

image-002.jpg (native tile, top, face A)
Left column, line ends (cut at left "]"):
  image-002 l.1  ]…̃   (only an abbreviation stroke at the top edge)
  image-002 l.2  ]n on   (the "n" is in darker/black ink, retraced?; then "on" with a stroke running off to the right: "nō"/"non"?)
  image-002 l.3  ]tē n(?)   ("]cē"/"]tē" with macron, then one or two minims at the fold)
  image-002 l.4  ]it ad   (or "]st ad"; red blot above the first letters)
  image-002 l.5  ]e miſ   ("]ē miſ" - e with stroke?, then "mis" with long s; a horizontal stroke after = line filler or abbreviation?)
  image-002 l.6  ]tres?   ("]tres"/"]ties"/"]tics"?)
  image-002 l.7  ]didiſſ?   ("]di" + "st"/"ſſ" ligature group: "]distiſ" / "]didiſſ"?)
  image-002 l.8  ]di an   (or "]di ar"/"]di au")
  image-002 l.9  ]tud?   ("]tuis"/"]ruis"/"]tud" - rubbed)
  image-002 l.10 ]… m…   (under a red patch; one stroke with macron; [illegible])
- Middle and right of the tile: blank, stained; no text. Red patches at right carry no letters.

image-003.jpg (native tile, upper-middle, face A; top overlaps the bottom of image-002)
Left column, line ends (cut at left "]"), pale brown ink, heavily rubbed and spattered red:
  image-003 l.1  ]tud?   (= image-002 l.9, overlap, not new text; "]ud"/"]uis" visible)
  image-003 l.2  ]…ar?   (= image-002 l.10, under red patch; "]m"/"]ar" + a long stroke to the right)
  image-003 l.3  ]… il / is?   (two dark vertical strokes at the fold in blacker ink, "il"/"ſſ"?; letters before them lost)
  image-003 l.4  ]… h? / li?   (one tall stroke only) [illegible]
  image-003 l.5  ]ndit? / ]ndr…   ("]nd" + 2 letters, with a long horizontal stroke above running to the right: "]ndit"/"]nder"?)
  image-003 l.6  ]pp? / ]ro?   (two rounded letters with loops; "]pp"/"]cco"?) [very uncertain]
  image-003 l.7  ]…ul / ]…ut?   (rubbed; a tall final letter at the fold)
  image-003 l.8  ]ſen / ]ſon? / ]den   (tall letter + "en", followed by a short stroke)
  image-003 l.9  ]…   (dark specks under red patch, c. 2-3 letters) [illegible]
- Middle zone: blank; a small faint mark near the hole (ghost of 2-3 letters or offset, unreadable). Right edge: red pigment band only, no letters in this tile. A column of short horizontal dashes down the right third = prickings/ruling marks (observation), about one per text line.

image-004.jpg (native tile, lower-middle, face A)
Left column, line ends - almost entirely lost under red pigment and abrasion:
  image-004 l.1  ]…   (dark specks, = image-003 l.9 overlap)
  image-004 l.2  ]… (a dark comma-shaped mark at the fold) [illegible]
  image-004 l.3  ]…y? / ]…r?   (on the stepped-out lower part of the left edge: one or two faint letters) [illegible]
  image-004 l.4  ]…a… o?   (faint brown, 3-4 letters, one rounded letter right of the fold) [illegible]
  image-004 l.5  ]…m?   [illegible]
  image-004 l.6-8  traces only; at the bottom "]… ll"/"]… u"? [illegible]
- Middle zone: a faint diagonal pencil/plummet-like scribble (later mark, not text). Prickings/dashes continue down the right third.
- Right edge, lowest part of tile: the first letter-beginnings of the right column appear, in brown ink, partly under red: one rounded letter "c"/"e"? at c. 80% height and another "c"? at the bottom edge.

image-005.jpg (native tile, bottom, face A; top overlaps image-004)
Left column, line ends (cut at left "]"), faint grey-brown under red patches:
  image-005 l.1  ]…   (under red, top) [illegible]
  image-005 l.2  ]m li? / ]n lr?   (minims + tall letter + i, at the fold; = bottom traces of image-004)
  image-005 l.3  ]…   (faint line, nothing certain) [illegible]
  image-005 l.4  ]r… / ]ſe…?   (a tall looped letter followed by one or two small letters and a dash)
  image-005 l.5  ]mu? / ]im?   (three or four minims)
  image-005 l.6  ]…   (under red) [illegible]
  image-005 l.7  ]er? / ]ec?   (two rounded letters)
  image-005 l.8  ]u? / ]il?   (bottom edge, strokes only)
Right column, line beginnings (cut at right "["), brown ink, ONE letter each, partly cut by the edge and under red:
  image-005 R1  e[ ?
  image-005 R2  c[ / e[ ?
  image-005 R3  t[ / c[ ?
  image-005 R4  p[ / v[ ?   (letter with a bowl; rubbed)
  image-005 R5  c[ / e[ ?
  image-005 R6  S   - a larger capital S (c. 2 lines' height in feel, plain brown ink, not coloured) set out to the LEFT of the column edge in the intercolumn/margin, with the first letter of its line (rubbed, "c"/"e"?) just right of it. Observation: an offset/hanging initial marking a new sentence or section.
  image-005 R7  [illegible, under red]
  image-005 R8  f[ / r[ ?   (tall letter)
  image-005 R9  d[
  image-005 R10 b[ / s[ ?   (at the bottom edge, darker)
- Middle: blank; holes and a horizontal slit (binding slots). Brown stain along the foot.

FACE A - AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
- All four native tiles (002-005) were examined in full; every visible line-end and line-beginning is listed. There is no connected prose on this face: the left column keeps only 2-6 letters per line and the right column one letter per line.

image-006.jpg (reduced overview, face B = other side of the same strip)
- Mirror layout: broad blank zone at left/centre with a vertical dark stain band and holes; a vertical fold c. 1 cm in from the RIGHT edge; right of the fold a column of line-BEGINNINGS in pale brown ink (c. 25 lines), cut by the right edge. At the far LEFT edge, lower half, faint line-ENDS of another column (1-3 letters each) under red pigment. Red patches along both edges.

image-007.jpg (native tile, top, face B)
Right column, line beginnings (cut at right "["), pale brown, rubbed:
  image-007 l.1  …na[ / nra[ ?   (first letters partly on the fold; "na" then a mark)
  image-007 l.2  iecer[ ? / ſcce[ ?   (starts with i/long-s, then "ece"/"cce" + r/t; a small superscript mark above the first letter)
  image-007 l.3  e(?) ſom[ / …ſlom[ ?   (a faint letter on the fold, then tall letter + "om"/"oni")
  image-007 l.4  lau[   ("lau" + minim: "laui"/"laun"/"laud"?)
  image-007 l.5  uoſ[ / iioſ[ ?   (minims + o + tall s/f)
  image-007 l.6  …m…[   (minims only: "inu"/"mm"?) [illegible]
  image-007 l.7  cſt[ / eſt[ ?   ("est" likely by shape, but faint)
  image-007 l.8  pop[ / rep[ ?   ("p" with descender twice?; at the stepped edge)
  image-007 l.9  [under red patch, illegible]
- Left edge of tile: red patches; one or two faint strokes at mid-height (line-end of the left column?), unreadable.

image-008.jpg (native tile, upper-middle, face B; top overlaps image-007)
Right column, line beginnings:
  image-008 l.1  pop[ / rep[ ?   (= image-007 l.8, overlap)
  image-008 l.2  [red patch] (= image-007 l.9)
  image-008 l.3  uor[ / por[ / uot[ ?   (rounded letters, "uo"/"po" + r)
  image-008 l.4  mа[ / ma[ / inc[ ?   (minims + a/c)
  image-008 l.5  a…[ / e…[ ?   (two small letters with a mark above) [illegible]
  image-008 l.6  utā[ / ucc̄[ ?   (letters with a macron: "utā"/"ucc"?)
  image-008 l.7  [faint, illegible]
  image-008 l.8  m…[ / in…[ ?   (minims + tall letter, near bottom)
  image-008 l.9  [traces at the bottom edge]
- Left edge: under red, faint line-ends of the left column at c. 45% and 58% height: single letters, "]r"? and "]ti"/"]h"? [illegible].

image-009.jpg (native tile, lower-middle, face B; top overlaps image-008)
Right column, line beginnings (cut at right "["), very pale:
  image-009 l.1  m…[ / in…[ ?   (= image-008 l.8, overlap; minims + tall letter)
  image-009 l.2  ſi…[ / fi…[ ?   (tall letter + minims) [very uncertain]
  image-009 l.3  …[   (minims, 2-3 letters) [illegible]
  image-009 l.4  [edge steps out here] 14c[ ? -> letters shaped "i" + tall "t"/"l" + "e/c": "ite"/"ile"/"rte"?   (first line on the wider lower part)
  image-009 l.5  im̄[ / uiē[ ?   (minims with a mark above; "ime"/"iniu"?)
  image-009 l.6  imp[ / mis[ / inf[ ?   (minims + a letter with descender or tall s)
  image-009 l.7  ab[ / al[ ?   (faint; rounded letter + tall letter)
  image-009 l.8  [under red patch, illegible]
  image-009 l.9  …[   (traces at the bottom edge)
Left column, line ends at the far left edge (under red, cut at left "]"): faint single letters at roughly five line levels - "]t"/"]r"?, "]t"?, "]i"?, "]x"/"]r"?, "]n"? - none secure. [illegible]

image-010.jpg (native tile, bottom, face B; top overlaps image-009)
Right column, line beginnings, mostly under red pigment:
  image-010 l.1  [red] 
  image-010 l.2  hou[ / bon[ / lou[ ?   (tall letter + "o" + minims, upper right, pale)
  image-010 l.3  [red]
  image-010 l.4  uo[ / no[ ?   (two letters between red patches)
  image-010 l.5  lab[ / leb[ / hil[ ?   (tall letter + rounded letter + tall letter)
  image-010 l.6  [red]
  image-010 l.7  …u[ ?   (one dark stroke right of a red patch)
  image-010 l.8-9  [red patches / traces only]
Left column, line ends at far left: nothing readable; red edge and brown staining. A faint "B"/"R"-like dark shape at the left edge c. 62% height is probably a line-end letter, unreadable.
- Middle: blank, surface cracked; holes and horizontal slit as on face A. Brown stain along the foot.

=====================================================================
SUMMARY FOR PACKET-05
=====================================================================

LAYOUT SURVEY
Observations
- One narrow vertical parchment strip, c. 4.5 x 21 cm, both faces supplied (face A: images 001-005; face B: images 006-010). Upright as presented on both faces.
- Each face shows a wide blank band (c. 2.5-3 cm) flanked by text: on face A, line-ENDS of a column at the left and single-letter line-BEGINNINGS of a column at the right; on face B the mirror image (line-ends at far left, barely visible; line-beginnings at right).
- A vertical fold with small holes (sewing?) runs c. 1 cm inside one long edge; a grey-brown vertical stain band runs down the middle of the blank zone, with several holes and horizontal slits (binding use).
- Short horizontal dashes in a vertical row on face A (right third) = prickings or ruling ticks, one per line.
- Script: a small, rounded, fairly informal bookhand in pale brown ink, c. 25-27 lines in the surviving height; a few letters on face A (l.2 "n", image-003 l.3) appear retraced in blacker ink.
- Only one enlarged letter: a plain brown capital "S" hanging in the margin left of the right column on face A (image-005 R6). No running title, rubric, coloured initial, underlining or gloss is visible. The bright red patches along the edges and in spots are smeared/offset pigment that overlies the text, not rubrication of this text (they carry no letter shapes).
Tentative interpretation
- The strip is the central part of a bifolium (the blank band = the two inner margins meeting at the spine fold) or the intercolumn of a two-column leaf; in either case only the outermost few letters of each column survive. A bifolium gutter seems likelier given the width of the blank band and the central stain/holes, but this cannot be settled from the images.

SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
- Every tile was examined in full. No heading, question opening or connected prose exists on the strip; the transcription is therefore a complete list of the line-edge fragments, given tile by tile above. The best-preserved run is face A, image-002 l.2-9 (eight consecutive line-ends) and face B, image-007 l.1-8 (eight consecutive line-beginnings).

Most secure readings (for later checking; all are fragments at a cut edge)
  Face A line-ends (image-002):  ]n on / ]tē n / ]it ad / ]e miſ / ]tres? / ]di…ſſ? / ]di an / ]tud?
  Face A (image-003):  ]nd…  / ]ſen (or ]den)
  Face A right column: initial letters only, incl. marginal capital S
  Face B line-beginnings (image-007):  …na[ / iece…[? / …ſom[? / lau[ / uoſ[? / … / est[? / pop[?
  Face B (image-008-010):  uor[? / ma[? / ut…[? / im…[ / imp[? / ab[? / uo[? / lab[?
None of these is long enough to be treated as a confirmed word; expansions were deliberately not supplied.

LIMITATIONS
- At most 2-6 letters per line on one side and 1-5 on the other; many are rubbed to ghosts or covered by red pigment. Readings marked "?" are shape-guesses.
- Recto/verso and the order of the columns across the two faces cannot be determined.
- Line numbers are counted per tile from the top of that image and overlap between adjacent tiles (noted where recognised); the total line count per face (c. 25-27) is approximate.
- Suggestion: raking-light or UV images of the left edge of face B and the left column of face A (lower half) might recover a few more letters; nothing wider exists to crop, since the images already show the whole strip.
